t.E333.agn: In 1973 JECFA set the ADI for citric acid and its calcium, potassium and sodium salts as 'not limited' and stated that these substances do not pose a significant toxicological risk to humans. JECFA reported that frequent or high intake of citric acid may cause dental erosion and local irritation because of its low pH.
t.E333.body: Citric acid and citrates occur naturally in many foods and are normal metabolic products in the body; citric acid takes part in the cells' energy cycle (the tricarboxylic acid cycle).
t.E333.eff.0.t: May cause erosion of tooth enamel and irritation in the mouth because of its low pH
t.E333.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E333.prod: Obtained by neutralising citric acid with calcium hydroxide or calcium carbonate.
t.E333.regx.0: ADI not limited (citric acid and its calcium, potassium and sodium salts).
t.E333.regx.1: Group I additive; permitted at quantum satis in many foods.
t.E333.summary: The calcium salts of citric acid. An acidity regulator, firming agent and source of calcium.
t.E333.what: A calcium salt that regulates the acidity of food, binds metal ions and helps firm texture.
